name: PLE page reclaim and prefetch admission
exact: Stored rows, IQ4_NL decoding, BF16 conversion and staging offsets are unchanged. CPU byte equality covers 200,000-position plain and MTP prefill/decode streams with the source mapping protected against reads. Native GPU token/logit/state and complete-workload qualification remain required for O_DIRECT rolling; GSQ page-drop behavior is not qualified.
gain: Capacity admission for T8192 at 128K/262K; no isolated speed attribution
preconditions: Linux, nonempty plain CLI prompt, tiled known prefill, registered file mapping, one valid IQ4_NL/BF16 PLE table with unregistered interior pages, verified setup drop and supported O_DIRECT reads. No model copy/promotion, graph, cohort, HTTP/serving, session load/live/follow-up, fixed MTP session or planned PLE IO. Plain prefix-cache restore/import and follow-up prompt routes retain the public prompt-wide planner; numerical snapshots never retain rolling source leases. Eager MTP retains required assets, explicit turn leases and phase-owned critical-first asynchronous prompt lookahead/c1 staging, with original offsets and turn/epoch/offset-validated pinned views. Calibration and decode drain the prompt pipeline, including pending staging tasks. Adaptive R2/R4/R8 row sets and min-p are covered by complete physical-window source leases including padding within the fixed decode quota; rejection/replay reuses or re-fetches owned bytes. Depth/survival controllers, copy-wide rows, golden dump, metadata-only, recording and sampled timing schedules remain excluded with specific inactive reasons. Cost-adaptive min-p schedules remain unchanged and require native token/logit/state qualification. Rolling uses owned aligned buffers with a shared 3 GiB default STRIX_PLE_ROLLING_CAP_BYTES cap plus fixed 256 MiB decode LRU and margin; allocation and inspection share admission arithmetic and separately charge metadata. Raw Linux io_uring uses 512 outstanding reads, a dedicated submission/completion thread and at most 128 KiB coalesced runs, without liburing. Unsupported setup/opcode detection (ENOSYS/EPERM/EINVAL) selects the checked O_DIRECT 32-thread pread fallback and reports its errno/backend. The setup helper completes each next-block read wave before later lookahead; critical demand promotes shared queued runs and pauses lookahead dispatch until critical completion. Small caps split ordered waves. STATS includes per-block critical bytes, completion-span application IOPS/MB/s and completed lookahead bytes. Plain c1/lookahead retains its original chunks and offsets, splitting/throttling under cap pressure. No rolling hot-path madvise/fadvise/mincore; table-wide residency is observed only at setup and drained request ends. Automatic setup failures tear down provisional owners, remove all credit and require fresh zero-credit resident admission before warming, retaining the MTP policy. Required mode refuses. Runtime read failures poison the source and exit nonzero; resident restart requires a fresh invocation.
off_switch: STRIX_PLE_RECLAIMABLE=0 disables reclaim. STRIX_PLE_ROLLING=0 or STRIX_CTX_EXACT_MEMORY=0 restores the previous plain prompt-wide mmap path and MTP warm path, ignoring rolling tuning.

name: PLE verify-window warming
exact: Exact by construction: warming never hands bytes to the window; it only loads pages the window's own rolling lease reads into the decode cache. Hashing, stored rows, IQ4_NL decoding, BF16 conversion, staging and GPU arithmetic are unchanged. Fixture strix-hip-ple-window-warm-tests compares windows with and without warming bitwise (R 1/2/4/8, edge/EOS/repeated tokens, wrong-token and stale-history warming, plain mapping and rolling turn); decode A/B token IDs identical.
gain: 1K-token MTP decode (G70), 2 interleaved rounds: code +1.1 %, code R8 +0.5 %, prose +1.0 %, prose R8 +1.0 %; traced R8 window PLE host gather 3.4 -> 0.87 ms.
preconditions: MTP decode with a rolling-residency decode turn; inert without one. The draft loop reports the pending token and each draft token after its step; rows are hashed from the last published n-gram history and their pages loaded by a background thread into the fixed 256 MiB decode cache. Wrong guesses only leave replaceable warm pages.
off_switch: STRIX_PLE_WINDOW_WARM=0 (also off with STRIX_QPF2K_DEFAULTS=0 or STRIX_BASELINE=1).

name: PLE decode pre-issue

Eager 1K/16K ON vs OFF: full logits and prompt/final target-state digests equal; token IDs equal in every timing arm.

preconditions: Plain CLI decode (no --mtp) with rolling residency, after the prompt is consumed. MTP sessions, verify windows, prompt blocks, HTTP serving, cohorts and distributed stages keep the plain path. Explicit setting refused on YaRN routes.
off_switch: STRIX_PLE_PREISSUE=0 (also off with STRIX_QPF2K_DEFAULTS=0 or STRIX_BASELINE=1, which win over an explicit =1).

name: Engram prefill projection tile with prefetch
exact: Bitwise: every output byte equals enqueue_f16_rows (rows 1..8192 incl. tile edges, padded strides with guard values, 3 independent F16 weight matrices, BF16-rounded inputs with signed zeros); same per-lane chains, separate multiply and add rounding, same butterfly and storing lane. 164 VGPR, no spill or scratch. Bitwise: fmaf(w, x, acc) equals acc + w * x when w is a finite F16 value and x is zero or a BF16 value with 2^-100 <= |x| < 2^101: the product is zero or has at most 19 significant bits and lies in 2^-124 .. 2^117, so it is exact and normal under any denormal mode (kernel built with IEEE denormals, float_denorm_mode_32 = float_denorm_mode_16_64 = 3). An infinite w gives the same infinity (or NaN against a zero x) in both forms; a NaN w gives NaN in both, payload bits may differ. A per-call scan flags any other x (Inf and NaN included) and the separate form runs instead; a stream under graph capture always takes the separate form. Gate: every output byte equal to enqueue_f16_rows and to STRIX_DS41_ENGRAM_PF_FMA=0 at rows 1..8192, forced tiles, and planted wide-x rows (2^-110, 2^110, subnormal products, non-BF16 values); scan classification asserted per category (signed zeros, 2^-100 and its BF16 neighbour, 2^101 and its BF16 neighbour, Inf, NaN, non-BF16 bits) at the first, middle and last element and with padded strides; full-mantissa x on which the unchecked fused form differs while every gated arm stays equal. Fused 48 x 64 kernel: 191 VGPR, no spill; 349 v_fmac / v_dual_fmac replace 304 multiplies and 281 adds.
gain: Isolated Engram projection (6144 -> 25600, event medians, interleaved arms, 3 weight copies) vs enqueue_f16_rows: rows 32 0.54x, 128 0.87x, 256 0.94x, 512 0.86x, 1024 0.86x (88.1 -> 75.8 ms), 2048 0.86x, 4096 0.86x, 8192 0.87x; 49..64 rows keep enqueue_f16_rows (64 rows: 1.16x). End-to-end TTFT not separately measured. With the separate form only (fused multiply-add off, graph capture, per-thread default stream), pieces of up to 2048 rows take a 48 x 32 tile of 512 threads (two workgroups resident per CU, 180 VGPR, no spill), same bits; separate-form timings: 1056 rows 0.998x, 2048 rows 0.992x of the 48 x 64 tile (3 rounds, 5-run medians); 8192 rows keep 48 x 64 (48 x 32 there 1.004x). STRIX_DS41_ENGRAM_PF_TILE=48 forces 48 x 64, =48x32 or =24 force those tiles (read per call). Exact fused multiply-add on the 48 x 64 tile: Isolated Engram projection, 4 weight copies, interleaved arms reversed every round, 5-run medians, two runs: 8192 rows 642.9 -> 613.6 ms and 648.6 -> 620.3 ms (-4.5 / -4.4 %) vs STRIX_DS41_ENGRAM_PF_FMA=0; forced 48 x 64 tile at 2048 rows -3.5 / -1.5 %. Pieces up to 2048 rows take the fused 48 x 64 tile as well: vs the separate 48 x 32 tile, 1056 rows 0.0 / -3.8 / -3.7 %, 2048 rows -2.4 / -3.6 / -3.3 % (three rounds); the separate-only route (FMA=0, graph capture, per-thread default stream) keeps 48 x 32 there. The 48 x 32 tile keeps the separate form (its fused body reaches 192 VGPR and spills: +10..12 %). About -0.11 s per rank at 32K, extrapolated from the isolated timing (8192-row pieces per rank derived from the prefill dispatch code, ~2.44 s of Engram projection per rank). End-to-end TTFT not separately measured.
preconditions: F16 Engram KV, full aligned view (width 6144, 25600 outputs, first 0, 16-byte aligned, valid strides), 32..8192 rows, row padding at most 9/8 of the 64-row tile (49..64 rows excluded); every other view keeps enqueue_f16_rows.
off_switch: STRIX_DS41_ENGRAM_F16_PF=0 (read on every call); STRIX_DS41_ENGRAM_PF_TILE=48 keeps the 48 x 64 tile at every row count; STRIX_DS41_ENGRAM_PF_FMA=0 keeps the separate multiply and add

Legacy idle/beside-decoder arms use the whole-prefill oracle for the long and both background requests. With a drafter loaded, only the legacy long request with a prompt of at most 4096 tokens fills Result::draft; legacy background requests and reorder/nested arms compare zero-initialized draft arrays. Short-first reorder uses FIFO standalone execution for both requests. Nested arms use standalone B1 for parent/child/background and check parked activations/checkpoints. All arms share prompt-output/first-head capture. Extended legacy/reorder coverage was requalified on GPU with this rule. Recorded GPU runs used complete 128-token continuations: legacy 1K prompt at 1/7/60-layer units idle and beside decoders, short-first reorder and 4608-token prompt, 11/11 IDENTICAL. Under HTTP load every request token ID is identical with policy ON and OFF.
gain: GPU, two Strix Halo nodes over 2x USB4 Gen3, PerfOpt kernel, MiniMax M3.1 Flash EXL3 3.06 bpw TP2; one binary built without a compiler cache, policy ON (default) and OFF (STRIX_MM_SERVE_SCHED=off) alternating inside each turn in both orders. Bursts submitted before any first token take OFF's operation path (one whole prefill per request, equal decode cycle counts); aggregate tok/s ON / OFF, two turns: distinct prompts C4 31.33/31.25 and 31.34/31.34, C8 36.28/36.10 and 36.48/36.61; identical prompts C8 43.74/43.78 and 43.81/42.79; total burst wall +0.05 % / -1.1 % (an earlier build of the rule: twelve alternating arms, mean 0.0 %). Mixed load (3 decoding streams x 384 tokens, then a 4539-token prompt, 183-token prompts 1 s and 3 s later), three turns ON / OFF: makespan 36.70/36.60, 35.69/35.67, 35.74/35.61 s (aggregate within 0.4 %); first short TTFT 1.13/12.69, 1.22/12.24, 1.24/12.19 s; second short, nested at a layer boundary of the long prompt, 1.11/11.60, 1.07/11.15, 1.11/11.09 s; decoders max chunk gap 2.08/15.72, 1.93/15.29, 1.94/15.28 s; long prompt TTFT 15.87/12.76, 15.13/12.34, 15.21/12.28 s (+19..24 %, its units yield to decoders; concurrent decode/prefill execution is in progress).
preconditions: Rank 0 protects only decoders whose first emission strictly predates the candidate submission. Without protection or warranted nesting, use FIFO whole prefill and admit again before decoding, exactly as OFF. Short-first requires a protected FIFO head. An older waiting short strictly predates both parent submission and prefill start; later shorts need their own protected decoder. Existing nesting size, bank, quota and deadline guards apply. Rank 1 replays rank 0; CPU traces compare full operation order and rows for 1/4/8 equal-time bursts. GPU re-measurement pending.

exact: Exact candidate: lossless versioned Q4_K prepared operands; existing affine certificate and existing fallback conversion, identical FP16 A/B and per-output ascending WMMA chains, incumbent epilogue/status/maxima and DA16 completion. Native byte gates and complete-workload qualification pending.

Tunes 80/88 use 256 threads and paired gate/up waves with permlanex16 B exchange. Tune 82 uses 512 threads and separate gate/up waves; half-wave replicas decode different adjacent K16 planes, exchange decoded FP16 fragments and execute them in ascending K order. Its epilogue rendezvous reuses A storage. Expected decode savings with small accumulator sets trade against register exchanges, duplicate compressed loads, repeated A operand reads and epilogue barriers; native verification pending. At most 160 VGPR, 20000 LDS bytes, zero scratch. CPU AMD Clang 22 gfx1151 resource inspection: 147/141 VGPR and 9/10 compiler waves/SIMD for tunes 80 or 88/82, 8960-18436 LDS bytes, no spills. Prepared asset identity includes layout version and verified model hash; additional packed allocations are charged in admission. Q5 formats, missing/mixed pairs, other shapes/routes/schedules decline. No native execution or speedup claim.
